title: Optimize walkthrough - Quantization profiles (INT8/FP8)
summary: Redwood AE+SE ran an Optimize walkthrough focused on quantization profiles (INT8 and FP8). Discussed accuracy regressions, latency improvements, hardware mapping and safe rollout strategies. Customer agreed to run a benchmark with Redwood-provided prompts and to evaluate INT8 on A100 and FP8 on H100. Next steps: share benchmark sheet, security docs, and schedule pilot kickoff.
next_steps: Alex to send benchmark spreadsheet + example prompts (by 2025-07-18)
Priya to share Optimize quant profiles guide and recommended hyperparameters (by 2025-07-17)
Customer to provision test capacity (A100 + H100) and share access plan (by 2025-07-22)
Schedule follow-up deep-dive to review results (week of 2025-07-28)
action_items: Alex Morgan; Send benchmark spreadsheet and latency/quality CSV; 2025-07-18
Priya Shah; Share quantization profiles guide (INT8/FP8 best practices); 2025-07-17
Jordan Lee; Provide sample prompt set and priority endpoints; 2025-07-20

transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-15 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~52 mins
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Papyrus - Head of ML), Samira Khan (Papyrus - Platform Eng), Liam O'Neill (Papyrus - CTO)
Artifacts referenced: Optimize deck (slides link: https://redwood.example.com/optimize-deck), benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), security FAQ (short link: https://redwood.example.com/security-faq)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intros, i'm alex from redwood, and priya is our se who will run through the optimize quant profiles walkthrough. Jordan, Samira, Liam, thanks for your time.
[00:18] Jordan: yeah thanks alex, we are excited — we want to get a clear read on INT8 vs FP8 for our retrieval + summarization flows, mostly lat sensitive.
[00:30] Priya: great, we'll cover recommended profiles, expected qps/latency wins, and where quality regressions commonly appear. We'll also show how rollout and evals fit into Optimize. Just a head's up, some of the terms in the deck are a bit terse — feel free to interrupt.
[00:48] Samira: quick note, our infra plan is mixed: dev on A100s in GCP, potential H100s on prem for inference, so we want guidance on hardware mapping.

[02:05] Priya: ok starting slide 1 — high level: INT8 gives strong latency and memory wins on many architectures but sometimes needs per-layer calibration; FP8 can be higher throughput on newer hw (H100/Hopper) and often preserves quality more than naive INT8 but it's more hardware dependent.
[02:40] Jordan: when you say "per-layer calibration" can you expand?
[02:45] Priya: sure — we run a small calibration pass using representative prompts; that shapes scale/zero points for symmetric/asymmetric quant. If you skip it, you often see clamp/saturation errors on attention weights, so quality drops. sometimes transcripts say "K V cash" instead of KV cache, haha, the transcriber hates that.
[03:12] Alex: quick disclaimer — numbers we'll show are representative; we'll provide the raw CSV in the spreadsheet so you can run the same tests.

[05:00] Priya: demo time — benchmark sheet up. baseline is FP16 on A100 with 512-token context. INT8 profile A reduces memory ~2x and median p99 latency improves by ~30% on A100. FP8 on H100 showed similar latency to INT8 but with smaller quality delta for our summarization prompts.
[05:40] Samira: do you have absolute token/sec numbers?
[05:45] Priya: yep, sheet has tokens/sec and p50/p90/p99; example: baseline FP16 p50 = 28ms/request, INT8 p50 = 19ms on the same rack w/ batch size 1, FP8 on H100 p50 = 18ms. these are for a 13B model.
[06:20] Liam: have you tried INT8 on H100? I’d expect even better.
[06:25] Priya: good question — INT8 on H100 often gains, but FP8 primitives on H100 are highly optimized by the compiler path we use; in some internal cases FP8 edges out INT8 due to lower compute cost per token. we'll share the exact kernel mapping in the doc.

[08:00] Jordan: what about quality — where do we see regressions?
[08:05] Priya: typical spots: long-tail token probabilities (rare proper nouns), arithmetic-like scoring tasks, and some fine-grained classification where logit shapes matter. For summarization specifically, INT8 can hallucinate slightly more on boundary sentences. We mitigate with per-prompt reranking or a fallback to FP16 for high-risk prompts.
[08:40] Alex: we also support automatic rollbacks: if Optimize detects a drop on your eval set it can route those calls to a higher-fidelity profile while keeping most traffic on the cheaper profile.

[10:05] Samira: can you show how to configure that in the Console?
[10:10] Priya: switching to Console: route rules, percent traffic on INT8 profile, canary windows, evaluation hooks. (screen share) here you see a traffic policy: 80% INT8, 20% FP16 for first 24 hours, run evals using your prompt set. If quality delta > threshold (we typically recommend >1.5% absolute drop), it can automatically revert.
[11:00] Jordan: how is the eval computed? are you running rouge/bleu or embedding similarity?
[11:05] Priya: we provide a pluggable eval harness. For summarization we recommend embedding-similarity on a human-curated gold set plus a few lexical metrics. We compute per-prompt delta and an aggregate score; thresholds are configurable.

[13:20] Alex: one question we often get — does caching and batching change measured gains?
[13:25] Priya: yes, absolutely. If you have a highly cacheable workload, raw per-token latency differences shrink because KV cache hits dominate. We include cache-aware measurements in the sheet. For uncached streaming workloads, INT8/FP8 wins are more pronounced.

[15:00] Jordan: curious about deterministic behavior. FP8 sometimes has more non-determinism?
[15:05] Priya: minor nondet can come from reduced precision accumulation and fused kernels; FP8 on some compilers uses different reduction orders. We recommend adding a small stochasticity budget to your evals — don't flag flakiness as regression unless it crosses a practical threshold.

[17:30] Samira: networking question — if we run on-prem H100 pool and Redwood hosted control plane, is there extra latency?
[17:35] Alex: for Private deployments we ship a control-plane that talks to your inference plane over private links. The request path for inference is local to the on-prem cluster so user-perceived latency matches local numbers; the control-plane calls are asynchronous and shouldn't affect inference p99. We'll share the diagram in the security FAQ.

[19:00] Priya: demo — show profile creation in Optimize: choose model, quant scheme, calibration sample size (we recommend 1-2k representative prompts), and target metrics. The UI also surfaces recommended profiles based on model & sequence length.
[20:10] Jordan: calibration sample size 1-2k — that could be heavy for us. any way to do lighter runs?
[20:15] Priya: yes, you can do progressive calibration: start with 200-500, inspect per-layer variance, then expand. For many models 500 representative prompts get you most of the win. We also provide heuristics built from our corpus.

[22:50] Liam: on the security side, we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration for keying model artifacts. Any caveats with quantized models?
[22:55] Alex: quantized model artifacts are encrypted at rest just like FP16; keys are managed through your KMS if you're on Private. We can document the HSM flow — Priya will attach the security doc.

[25:10] Priya: quick aside on mixed precision: sometimes we choose mixed INT8/FP16 per-layer — e.g., keep attention kernels in FP16 and quantize feedforward. That hybrid often gives most of the latency wins with fewer quality regressions. We call those "profile B" or similar in the sheet.

[27:00] Jordan: do you have recommended thresholds for rollback? we don't want to be hypersensitive.
[27:05] Priya: recommend aggregate score delta >1% or per-critical-prompt delta >2% for automated rollback. But we tune per workload. The Console also has a dry-run mode where you can simulate traffic without affecting production.

[29:30] (short crosstalk)
[29:45] Samira: one more infra nit — concurrency. our current endpoints have 8 concurrent streams. how should we size batcher and prefetch?
[29:50] Priya: general rule: for streaming low-latency workloads keep batch size 1-4 and optimize prefetch to fill GPU without adding head-of-line latency. Our autotuner can suggest values from a short calibration run. We'll include suggested configs per profile in the guide.

[32:00] Priya: back to bench results — show quality vs latency curve for the 13B model: curve shows INT8 gives 25-35% latency win with 0.5-1.8% quality delta depending on prompt class; FP8 tends to sit slightly right of INT8 on latency but closer in quality.
[32:40] Jordan: can we get raw logits or confidence scores to build a reranker?
[32:45] Alex: yes, Redwood's API returns logits/probs if you enable that — cost implications noted in the docs. Priya: note that quantized kernels may slightly shift logits; rerankers should be trained or calibrated on quantized outputs.

[35:10] Liam: any surprises moving from 13B to 70B?
[35:15] Priya: scale changes dynamics: 70B often sees larger memory wins from INT8 but also larger potential for quality drift. For big models FP8 is increasingly attractive because it reduces memory and keeps numeric range. We recommend a staged approach: start INT8 on smaller models, then validate on larger ones.

[37:30] Jordan: how long does calibrate + benchmark typically take?
[37:35] Priya: calibration couple hours for 2k prompts on a single GPU; end-to-end benchmark across your full prompt set maybe a day depending on parallelism. The spreadsheet we share has sample run-times so you can estimate cost.

[39:10] Alex: question from the chat — competitor note: how is this different from what Anthropic or AWS offers?
[39:15] Priya: short answer: we focus on a production-first orchestration + Optimize tooling that ties quantization, rollout, and evals together with per-route cost visibility. Other vendors may offer primitives but not the same integrated rollouts + automatic fallbacks.

[41:40] Samira: want to call out a potential blocker: our compliance team wants audit logs for any automatic routing decisions. is that available?
[41:45] Alex: yes, we produce audit trails for rollouts and automated rollbacks; entries include eval snapshot, timestamp, and the traffic slices affected. We'll attach sample logs.

[43:30] Priya: live Q/A — Jordan: do you recommend enabling model distillation before quantization?
[43:35] Priya: distillation can help, but it changes model behavior; often teams prefer quantization first and only distill if you need extra headroom. Distilled-then-quantized models can be tricky to debug.

[45:10] Jordan: if we hit a quality regression, what are remediation options?
[45:15] Priya: options: increase calibration sample size, use hybrid profile (keep sensitive layers in FP16), bump to FP8 on H100, or enable per-prompt reranking/fallback. Also can tune generation params (temperature/top-k) which sometimes reduces hallucinations.

[47:40] Liam: let's talk runbook — we want a clear pilot path.
[47:45] Alex: suggested pilot: 1) Redwood shares benchmark sheet + suggested profiles, 2) Papyrus runs A100 INT8 and H100 FP8 tests against the provided prompts, 3) we review results and pick profile for a 2-week canary with 20% traffic, 4) expand or rollback based on evals. We can also do a Redwood-assisted benchmark where we run tests if you provide access.

[50:10] Priya: last quick notes — watch out for prompt truncation interactions with quantized KV caches; we include guardrails in our runtime that check cache keys and sequence alignment. Also, quantized artifacts are versioned and you can pin model+profile combos in the Console.

[51:05] Alex: recap — action items: we'll send spreadsheet, priya will attach the guide, customer will share prompt set and infra plan. Any final q's?
[51:20] Jordan: nope, sounds good. thanks all.
[51:30] Liam: thanks, appreciate the practical guidance.
[51:40] Meeting end.
